div.head: ECf retr Rb XXII
div.ab: Quid sit fridborch, quod soli Eboracenses uocant tenmentale, id est sermo decem hominum.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 671 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

This is one of the chapter headings (rubrics) that a later writer, whom Liebermann calls “Rubricator II” and dates 1163–1189, made for the Retractator’s text; so the date given for ECf retr (c. 1140–59) does not apply to it. Liebermann prints them on pp. 670–672 as an appendix (Anhang) to ECf retr; they are numbered here “Rb” with his Roman numerals. He prints in small type what is taken from the text of ECf retr, so the words in bold are the Rubricator’s own.
Liebermann gives in the margin, in square brackets, the chapter of ECf retr that this heading belongs to: 20.
Liebermann puts note 18 on the numeral; here it stands at the start of the heading. He prints note 19 both after “fridborch” and after “tenmentale”.
div.ab: What fridborch (frankpledge) is, which the men of York alone call tenmentale, that is, the speech of ten men.
